card.title: Make a branch and work on it
card.blurb: Split off a line of work and commit on it without touching `main`. Make a branch, step onto it, and watch the graph fork while the old line stays put.
hero.title: Make a branch and work on it
intro.0: You want to try something without risking the work that already runs, so you split off a second line with its own name. Nothing is copied - a branch is only a name pointing at a commit. Here you make one, step onto it, and commit there while `main` stays where you left it.
task.1.title: Name a second line of work
task.1.context:
A branch is a name pointing at a commit. `git branch feature` makes that name where you are standing.

It can also point further back. `HEAD~1` is the commit before `HEAD` and `HEAD~3` is three before it, so `git branch old HEAD~3` names a commit you are not on. `git log --oneline` tells you which one that is.
task.1.goal.0: Run `git log --oneline` and find the commit whose message is `add dog`.
task.1.goal.1: Make a branch called `feature` at that commit. On its own, `git branch feature` would put it at `HEAD`.
task.1.goal.2: Stay on `main` - run `git branch` and check the `*` is still there.
task.2.title: Step onto it and commit there
task.2.context:
`git switch feature` moves `HEAD` onto that branch, so your next commit lands there. `git switch -c feature` does both jobs at once: make the name, then step onto it.

The new branch starts where you are standing, so check where that is first - `git branch` marks the current one with a `*`.
task.2.goal.0: Run `git branch` - it marks the branch you are on with a `*`.
task.2.goal.1: The dog's work belongs on a new branch called `feature`, growing from `main`.
task.2.goal.2: Make `feature` and step onto it with `git switch -c feature` - it starts where you are standing, so be standing in the right place.
task.2.goal.3: Stage `dog.txt` and save it with `git commit -m "add dog"`.
task.3.title: Make a branch and work on it - recap
task.3.context: A name, and the marker that says which name you are on.
task.3.summaryIntro: Branching costs nothing, because there is nothing to copy. You add a name, you decide whether to stand on it, and from then on your commits go where you are standing.
task.3.summaryItems.0.title: Branch -
task.3.summaryItems.0.text: a name pointing at a commit, moving forward with you as you commit on it.
task.3.summaryItems.1.title: `HEAD` -
task.3.summaryItems.1.text: the marker for where you are, so it decides which branch your next commit lands on.
task.3.summaryItems.2.title: `git branch feature` -
task.3.summaryItems.2.text: makes the name where you are standing, or further back with `HEAD~2`, and leaves you where you were.
task.3.summaryItems.3.title: `git switch -c feature` -
task.3.summaryItems.3.text: makes it and steps onto it, so the work that follows grows on the new line.
task.3.summaryClose: Next: tags - a name that pins one commit and never moves again.
meta.label: Branches · Make a branch and work on it
concept.gt-revision.def: A way to name a commit without its hash - `HEAD`, a branch name, or a step back from one like `HEAD~1`.
